title: A height-one prime above a principalized local maximal ideal
statement: Let $B\subseteq S$ be an inclusion of commutative nonzero integral domains. Assume that $B$ is local with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$, and that $S$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $0\ne a\in\mathfrak m_B$ and assume $\mathfrak m_BS=aS\ne S$, where $\mathfrak m_BS$ is the ideal of $S$ generated by $\mathfrak m_B$. There exists a prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ minimal over $aS$ such that $\mathfrak q\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$ and $\operatorname{ht}_S(\mathfrak q)=1$. Here minimal over $aS$ means $aS\subseteq\mathfrak q$ and there is no prime $\mathfrak p$ with $aS\subseteq\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$; height is the supremum of the lengths $n$ of finite strict chains $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n\subseteq\mathfrak q$ of prime ideals of $S$.

source.place: Tag 00P8, algebra-lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof sentences choosing a minimal prime over x_r S, proving height one, and proving that it lies over the original maximal ideal (original item steps 4-5).

proof.text: Since $aS\ne S$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal] with $\Lambda=S$ and $I=aS$. Obtain a prime $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $aS$, in particular $aS\subseteq\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 00P8, algebra-lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof, lines 28913-28918, expanded for the stated B ⊆ S hypotheses. Existence is Algebra Tag 00E0, algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology, parts (2) and (4).

proof.text: The contraction $J=\mathfrak q\cap B$ is an ideal of $B$: closure under addition and multiplication by $B$ follows from the corresponding closure of $\mathfrak q$ in $S$. It is proper because $1\notin\mathfrak q$. Every $b\in\mathfrak m_B$ maps into $\mathfrak m_BS=aS\subseteq\mathfrak q$, hence $\mathfrak m_B\subseteq J$. Maximality of $\mathfrak m_B$ and properness of $J$ give $J=\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 00P8, algebra-lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof, lines 28913-28918, expanded for the stated B ⊆ S hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-krull-principal-ideal-height-bound] with $R=S$, $x=a$, and the minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ from step 1. The ring $S$ is Noetherian by hypothesis and $aS=(a)$ is principal, so $\operatorname{ht}_S(\mathfrak q)\leq1$.

source.place: Tag 00KV, algebra-lemma-minimal-over-1, part (1), as invoked in Tag 00P8.

proof.text: The inclusion $B\subseteq S$ preserves $a\ne0$, and $a\in aS\subseteq\mathfrak q$, so $\mathfrak q\ne(0)$. Since $S$ is a nonzero domain, $(0)$ is a prime ideal (if $uv=0$, then $u=0$ or $v=0$). Thus $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ is a strict prime chain of length one, giving $\operatorname{ht}_S(\mathfrak q)\geq1$ directly from the definition of height in the statement. Together with step 3 this gives height exactly one. Step 1 supplies minimality and step 2 the required contraction, completing all clauses.
